captions.instagram:
How does a guitar work?

Six strings pulling with 73 kg, a thin spruce top that pumps the air, and a magnet that hears steel move. Pluck, fret and strum a guitar in 3D, then plug it in and push the amp until it clips.

→ A guitar is six strings, a neck with frets, and a hollow wooden box.
→ An electric swaps the hollow box for a solid body and magnetic pickups.
→ A plucked string swings as a whole, and in halves, thirds and quarters at once.
→ Pluck it in the middle and every even harmonic goes missing: a softer, rounder note.
→ Each fret shortens the string by the same 5.6%, so the 12th fret sits exactly halfway.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/guitarclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a guitar work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Six strings pulling with 73 kg, a thin spruce top that pumps the air, and a magnet that hears steel move. Pluck, fret and strum a guitar in 3D, then plug it in and push the amp until it clips.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/guitarclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/guitarclear

In this video:
• Six strings between two points. A guitar's strings run from the saddle on the bridge to the nut at the top of the neck.
• Where you pluck changes the tone. A plucked string vibrates as a whole and in halves, thirds and quarters at once.
• Frets divide the octave into twelve. Each fret shortens the vibrating string by the same factor, 2^(−1/12) ≈ 0.944, which raises the note one semitone.
• The body does the shouting. A string alone is almost silent, because air slips around it.
• A pickup is Faraday's law. An electric guitar's pickup is a magnet inside a coil of about 8,000 turns of fine wire.
• Distortion is clipping on purpose. An amplifier makes the pickup's signal many times bigger.
